editorial:
Imagine spending your days working at a crematory, surrounded by death and old ghosts. You get a front-row seat to a spooky setting where things go wrong very quickly. The movie puts you right in the middle of a creepy Taiwanese town where the line between the living and the dead is thin. You will follow characters who are just trying to do their jobs, but they end up dealing with spirits that have some serious grudges. The vibe is heavy and dark, making you feel like something is watching from every corner of the room.

What really works here is how the movie builds tension without using too many big special effects. The acting feels real, and the slow build-up makes the scares hit harder. Some parts might feel a bit slow if you like non-stop action, but the payoff is worth it. If you love old-school Asian horror, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the ghosts finally reveal why they are angry. You find out that greed and betrayal caused the deaths in the first place. The main characters have to face the spirits in a final showdown at the crematory. In the end, the ghosts get the justice they wanted, and the bad people get what they deserve. It wraps up with a clear lesson that you cannot hide your sins forever.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old Asian ghost stories and gothic settings.
